summary: Lensk Airport serves the town of Lensk in the Sakha Republic of eastern Siberia, Russia, providing vital connectivity to this remote region along the Lena River. As a medium-sized regional airport, it supports both passenger services and plays a role in supporting the local diamond mining industry that drives the area's economy. The airport operates under challenging climatic conditions typical of Yakutia, with extreme winter temperatures.
faqs:
Q: What is the IATA code for Lensk Airport?
A: The IATA code is ULK, and the ICAO code is UERL.

Q: Where is Lensk located?
A: Lensk is situated in the Sakha Republic (Yakutia) in eastern Siberia, along the Lena River, one of the longest rivers in the world.

Q: When is the best time to fly to Lensk?
A: Summer months from June to August offer the most comfortable travel conditions, as winter temperatures in Yakutia can drop well below -40°C.

Q: What industries does Lensk serve?
A: The airport primarily serves the local community and the diamond mining industry, as Lensk is near significant diamond deposits operated by ALROSA.
transport_tips: The airport is located near the town of Lensk and can be reached by taxi or local transport within a short drive. There are no rail connections to Lensk, so air and river transport are the primary ways to access the town during much of the year. In winter, an ice road across the Lena River may provide additional ground access to nearby settlements.
local_tip: Pack layered clothing even in summer — nighttime temperatures in the Sakha Republic can be surprisingly cold due to the continental subarctic climate, and weather can shift rapidly between seasons.
